summary: Heights, rational points and obstructions, planned at target level from the pinned libraries. RP.0 builds heights over Conrad's generalized global fields, expressed through Mathlib's Height.AdmissibleAbsValues (number fields and polarized function fields alike): the normalised projective height, its extension invariance and Northcott for bounded degree, Weil's height machine on Pic(X) with values in the existing quotient of functions modulo bounded ones, Tate's limit as a real-bodied lemma, the Néron–Tate height of any line bundle on an abelian variety with its kernel (Northcott only), bilinear form and local Néron functions, the Silverman–Tate and Silverman specialization theorems in families, and canonical heights of subvarieties over function fields (Xie–Yuan, Gubler). RP.1 instantiates the EllipticCurves Layer 7 Selmer-structure API for abelian varieties: Kummer maps of isogenies (fppf, Galois when the degree is invertible), local unramified images, Selmer and Tate–Shafarevich groups, the descent sequence, finiteness, weak Mordell–Weil and Mordell–Weil through Mathlib's descent theorem, positive definiteness, the K/k-trace and Lang–Néron with the function-field kernel, and Bhargava–Gross–Wang two-coverings and Selmer sets. RP.2 extends the affine checkpoint to adelic points of separated schemes, scheme Brauer classes (key/scheme-brauer), local constancy, the general Brauer–Manin pairing and set, functoriality, algebraic, unramified and B_ω Brauer groups, the zero-cycle pairing, the formal lemma, cyclic norm classes, Brauer groups of complete intersections, and worked conics and Iskovskikh's surface with an effective finite test. RP.3 plans torsor descent (Poonen §8.4–8.6): evaluation and twisting, the descent partition, Selmer sets, descent and étale–Brauer sets with their comparisons, universal torsors, Harpaz–Wittenberg's unramified descent for torus torsors, genus-one torsors and Weil–Châtelet, and the insufficiency examples. RP.4 plans the Kodaira–Parshin construction, de Franchis, Parshin's implication, Chevalley–Weil and Siegel's theorem. RP.5 plans abelian subvarieties, stabilizers, the Ueno locus, finite-rank groups, Manin–Mumford (all characteristics), Faltings' subvariety theorem, Vojta's inequality and Mumford's gap principle, Mordell–Lang, the Faltings–Zhang map and the Ullmo–Zhang Bogomolov theorem. RP.6 plans local solubility, the Abel–Jacobi transfer, the genus classification and a register of the open conjectures. Requests go to Tau Ceti roadmaps (ClassFieldTheory, EllipticCurves, GlobalQuadraticForms, JacobianChallenge), FaltingsFinitenessAndIsogenyTheorems R28.5 and SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.2; gaps record the arithmetic intersection theory behind equidistribution and the cited deep proofs of RP.5.

readSections: Read physical/printed pp.1–3 and 6–10: goals and elementary heights; coordinate estimates; all of §14, including its footnote and Steps 1–7; local-function discussion and §17. Pages 4–5 and 11–13 are not claimed read. Pages 2,6,8,9 were visually checked for the recorded source findings. The quotient and finiteness interfaces below use §14 footnote and §17 as motivation, with their elementary proofs written here. No claim that the notes prove the complete roadmap.

Authorship and course context verified at https://www.math.columbia.edu/~dejong/courses/schemes-spring-2022.html. No dated revision or separate correction located on that page or the author homepage on 2026-09-27.

nodes.title: Uniform boundedness at the top filter
nodes.statement: For h:X→ℝ, membership in the native boundedFilterSubmodule at the top filter is equivalent to the existence of C≥0 such that |h(x)|≤C for every x∈X.
hypotheses: X, Y and Z are arbitrary types, with no topology or nonemptiness assumption; all functions take real values. Additional assumptions are stated explicitly.
proofSteps: Unfold native boundedFilterSubmodule and BoundedAtFilter. Asymptotics.isBigO_top changes the filter statement into one bound for every x, since the norm of the constant real one is one.
Replace a possibly negative bound C by max(C,0). This also handles X empty without a nonemptiness assumption. Conversely forget nonnegativity and use the native top-filter equivalence.
acceptance: On the empty type C=0 works.
The alternating sequence (−1)^n has bound 1.
The sequence n on the natural numbers has no uniform bound.

nodes.title: Heights modulo bounded functions
nodes.statement: For any type X, HeightClass(X) is the native real module quotient of the function space X→ℝ by Filter.boundedFilterSubmodule at the top filter. Write [h] for the native linear quotient projection. It is a real vector space; no topology or pointwise evaluation of a class is supplied.
hypotheses: X, Y and Z are arbitrary types, with no topology or nonemptiness assumption; all functions take real values. Additional assumptions are stated explicitly.
proofSteps: Specialize the native bounded-function submodule to real-valued functions and the top filter, then use the native submodule quotient. This is a transparent abbreviation, not another quotient relation or another boundedness predicate.

Use the inherited quotient module structure and mkQ. Constants belong to the submodule by const_boundedAtFilter, so their classes vanish. On a finite type every real function has a finite, hence bounded, range. The native metric boundedness criterion at center zero gives the Bornology compatibility statement.
For linear descent use native liftQ with the exact kernel-inclusion hypothesis; liftQ_apply and quot_hom_ext supply its computation and uniqueness interfaces.
acceptance: Bounded nonconstant functions vanish.
A pointwise product of two classes is not defined: [1]=[0], but [n·1]≠[n·0].
Finite point sets give the zero quotient.

nodes.title: The bounded-error equality criterion
nodes.statement: For h,g:X→ℝ, [h]=[g] if and only if there is a real C≥0 such that |h(x)−g(x)|≤C for every x.
hypotheses: X, Y and Z are arbitrary types, with no topology or nonemptiness assumption; all functions take real values. Additional assumptions are stated explicitly.
proofSteps: Use native Submodule.Quotient.eq to replace equality by membership of h−g in the bounded-function submodule.
Apply uniform-boundedness and evaluate subtraction pointwise. The bound is uniform over the whole chosen point type, not merely pointwise finite or bounded on a separately chosen finite subset.
acceptance: [2n]≠[n] on ℕ.
Equality of classes does not imply equality of values at a point.

nodes.title: Pullback of height classes
nodes.statement: For any function f:X→Y, pullback(f):HeightClass(Y)→HeightClass(X) is the real linear map induced by precomposition: [h]↦[h∘f]. For X→Y→Z, pullback(g∘f)=pullback(f)∘pullback(g). No finite-fiber assumption is needed to define this map.
hypotheses: X, Y and Z are arbitrary types, with no topology or nonemptiness assumption; all functions take real values. Additional assumptions are stated explicitly.
proofSteps: Form the native precomposition linear map from LinearMap.pi and LinearMap.proj: its x-coordinate is evaluation at f(x).
If h is bounded by C everywhere on Y, h∘f has the same bound on X. By uniform-boundedness this is exactly the submodule compatibility required by native mapQ.

Use native mapQ with that compatibility proof. Its evaluation, identity and composition theorems give the representative formula and contravariant functor laws. Constant f produces a constant representative, hence the zero map.
acceptance: On ℕ, pullback of [n] along doubling is 2[n].
Pullback along a constant map is zero.
Composition reverses order.

nodes.title: Surjective maps detect height classes
nodes.statement: If f:X→Y is surjective, pullback(f):HeightClass(Y)→HeightClass(X) is injective.
hypotheses: X, Y and Z are arbitrary types, with no topology or nonemptiness assumption; all functions take real values. Additional assumptions are stated explicitly.
proofSteps: Choose representatives h and g for two classes, using native mkQ_surjective. The definition through mapQ says equality of pullbacks is equality of [h∘f] and [g∘f].
Use equality-criterion to obtain C bounding |h(f(x))−g(f(x))| on all X. For each y choose an x with f(x)=y; the same C bounds the difference on Y.
Apply equality-criterion on Y. No finiteness of the fibers is used.
acceptance: A bijection gives an isomorphism through its inverse pullback.
Projection ℕ×ℕ→ℕ is surjective and detects classes even though it does not preserve Northcott finiteness.

nodes.title: Northcott transfer under a lower comparison
nodes.statement: Let h,g:X→ℝ and C∈ℝ satisfy h(x)≤g(x)+C for every x. If h is Northcott in the native sense, then g is Northcott.
hypotheses: X, Y and Z are arbitrary types, with no topology or nonemptiness assumption; all functions take real values. Additional assumptions are stated explicitly.
proofSteps: Fix a real B. If g(x)≤B, then h(x)≤B+C. Thus the B-sublevel set of g is a subset of the (B+C)-sublevel set of h.
Apply native Northcott.finite_le and finite-set subset closure. This constructs the native Northcott instance for g; it introduces no second finiteness predicate.
acceptance: Take h(n)=n and g(n)=n+(−1)^n, with C=1.
The reversed inequality is insufficient: 0≤n on ℕ, while n is Northcott and the constant zero function is not.

sources.match: Explicit elementary sublevel-set proof supplying the representative interface for the finiteness notion used by the source. No projective Northcott theorem is re-planned.

nodes.title: Northcott invariance under bounded error
nodes.statement: If h,g:X→ℝ have equal height classes, then native Northcott(h) holds if and only if native Northcott(g) holds.
hypotheses: X, Y and Z are arbitrary types, with no topology or nonemptiness assumption; all functions take real values. Additional assumptions are stated explicitly.
proofSteps: Use equality-criterion to choose C≥0 with |h(x)−g(x)|≤C for every x. The absolute-value inequality gives both h(x)≤g(x)+C and g(x)≤h(x)+C.

n and −n on ℕ are not boundedly equivalent; only the first is Northcott.

On a fixed field, this transfers an imported arithmetic-height finiteness theorem to any boundedly equal geometric representative. It does not assert finiteness over an algebraic closure without a degree restriction.

nodes.title: Generalized global fields
nodes.statement: A generalized global field is a field K with an admissible family of absolute values in the sense of Mathlib's Height.AdmissibleAbsValues K (a finite multiset of archimedean absolute values counted with multiplicity, a set of nonarchimedean ones, finite support of every nonzero element, and the product formula), such that every nonarchimedean member is discretely valued with excellent valuation ring. A finite extension K'/K inside a fixed algebraic closure receives the extended family by the algebraic method: each v extends to the finitely many w | v, normalised so that the restriction of the w-absolute value to K is the v-absolute value raised to [K'_w : K_v]·e_v/e_w (e = 2 at complex places, 1 otherwise). The extended family again satisfies the product formula, and the construction is transitive in towers.
hypotheses: K a field; the archimedean multiplicity convention is Mathlib's: a complex place occurs twice in the multiset, which is Conrad's exponent e_v = 2.
Excellence of the nonarchimedean valuation rings is automatic in characteristic 0.
proofSteps: Take Conrad's Definition 8.1 and encode the family as Mathlib's AdmissibleAbsValues, so that the product formula and finite support are Mathlib's axioms.

Extension: K' ⊗_K K_v is reduced (separability of K_v/K, from excellence), so it splits as the product of the K'_w; the norm formula gives the product formula for the extended family (Conrad §8, display before Example 8.5).
Transitivity in towers follows from multiplicativity of local degrees.
acceptance: For K = ℚ with Mathlib's instance the product formula at x = 2 reads 2 · (1/2) = 1.
The extended family on a number field K' is Mathlib's own instance on K' (Conrad Example 8.5).

sources.locator: §8, Definition 8.1 and the algebraic method for finite extensions, author copy pp. 27–29
sources.match: Defines generalized global fields by a product-formula family of absolute values with discrete excellent nonarchimedean members, and extends such a structure canonically through finite extensions.
The arithmetic case is a number field with its normalised absolute values; the algebraic method recovers the normalised absolute values of a finite extension.

uses.how: heights over K̄ are normalised through the extended families on finite subextensions
the geometric heights of a finitely generated field K/k are heights for such a structure (model-mk-height)
the projective height is defined for any generalized global field

nodes.title: Polarized function fields as generalized global fields
nodes.statement: Let k be a field, K/k a finitely generated extension with k algebraically closed in K and trdeg_k K ≥ 1, and (V, N) a polarization: V a normal projective k-variety with function field K and N an ample line bundle on V. For each prime divisor D of V put |x|_D = exp(−deg_N(D)·ord_D(x)) with deg_N(D) = (c₁(N)^{dim V−1}·D). These absolute values make K a generalized global field (all nonarchimedean). The elements with |x|_D = 1 for every D are exactly the nonzero constants k^×. If K'/K is finite with normalisation V' of V in K', constant field k' and pulled-back N', the algebraic-method family on K' is the (V', N') family raised to the power [k' : k].
hypotheses: k algebraically closed in K; V normal (regular in codimension one suffices) and projective; N ample.
When dim V = 1, V is unique and deg_N(D) = [k(D) : k] does not depend on N.
proofSteps: The product formula is the vanishing of deg_N of a principal divisor (Conrad Example 8.4), via SF.5 intersection numbers: deg_N(div f) = c₁(N)^{dim V−1}·div f = 0.
Finite support: a nonzero rational function has finitely many zero and polar divisors.
Extension: Conrad Lemma 8.6 compares the two families through leading coefficients of Hilbert polynomials (projection formula for the finite map V' → V).
acceptance: For V = ℙ²_k, N = O(1) and f = q/x² with q a smooth conic, the weighted orders are 2·1 − 1·2 = 0 while the unweighted orders sum to −1.

sources.locator: §8, Example 8.4 and Lemma 8.6, author copy pp. 27–29
sources.match: The geometric case: weights e^{−deg_{k,N}(v)} on codimension-one points of a normal projective model give the product formula; Lemma 8.6 compares the algebraic-method extension with the model of the normalisation, with exponent [k':k].

nodes.title: The normalised projective height
nodes.statement: For a generalized global field K with algebraic closure K̄ and n ≥ 0, h_{K,n} : ℙⁿ(K̄) → ℝ_{≥0} sends [t₀ : … : t_n] with t_i in a finite subextension K'/K to [K':K]^{-1}·Σ_{w} log max_i |t_i|_w^{e_w} (sum over the extended family of K'). It does not depend on K', on the homogeneous coordinates, or on the choice of K̄, and it is Aut(K̄/K)-invariant. For x ∈ ℙⁿ(K) it equals Mathlib's Projectivization.logHeight over K. For K = ℚ it is the absolute logarithmic Weil height h on ℙⁿ(ℚ̄); for x ∈ ℙⁿ(L) with L a number field, [L:ℚ]·h(x) is Mathlib's logHeight over L, and h([x : 1]) = NumberField.absLogHeight₁ x.
hypotheses: K a generalized global field; the coordinates lie in a finite subextension.
proofSteps: Independence of K' from Σ_{w''|w}[K''_{w''}:K'_w] = [K'':K'] (Conrad §9).
Independence of coordinates from the product formula (Mathlib Height.mulHeight_smul_eq_mulHeight over K').
Galois invariance: σ permutes the places of σK' preserving local degrees.

sources.locator: §9, definition of h_{K,n} (first display of §9) and Remark 9.1, author copy pp. 29–30
sources.match: The standard K-height on ℙⁿ(K̄) normalised by [K':K], independent of K' and invariant under Aut(K̄/K); in the arithmetic case one divides by [K:ℚ] to get an absolute height.
The absolute number-field projective height with the [K':ℚ]^{-1} normalisation, squared complex absolute values, and its independence of coordinates and of the field.
Uses the absolute coordinate height of algebraic points with bounded degree.

uses.how: the absolute height of algebraic points entering the arithmetic bigness comparisons
heights of CM coordinates of bounded degree
normalisation: very ample heights are pullbacks of h_{K,n}

nodes.title: Heights under finite extension of the base field
nodes.statement: Let K be a generalized global field and K'/K finite with the extended structure. For x ∈ ℙⁿ(K), Mathlib's logHeight of x over K' equals [K':K] times its logHeight over K; equivalently h_{K',n} = [K':K]·h_{K,n} on ℙⁿ(K̄). For a projective K-variety X and a line bundle L, [K':K]·h_{K,L} = h_{K',L_{K'}} as classes on X(K̄).
hypotheses: K'/K finite; K' carries the structure of generalized-global-field (extend).
proofSteps: For v on K: Σ_{w|v} [K'_w:K_v] = [K':K] (reducedness of K' ⊗ K_v).
For x ∈ K, log|x|_w^{e_w} = [K'_w:K_v]·log|x|_v^{e_v} by extend_restrict; summing over w | v and then over v gives the identity.
For line bundles, apply it to very ample embeddings and use additivity (Conrad (9.2)).
acceptance: For K = ℚ, K' = ℚ(i) and x = [2:1], the two sides are 2·log 2.

sources.match: States [K':K]·h_{K,L} = h_{K',L_{K'}} on X(K̄) modulo bounded functions.

nodes.title: Coordinate heights of algebraic tuples
nodes.statement: For algebraic numbers x₁, …, x_m ∈ ℚ̄ with absolute logarithmic heights h(x_i) = NumberField.absLogHeight₁ x_i: max_i h(x_i) ≤ h([1 : x₁ : … : x_m]) ≤ Σ_i h(x_i). For x ∈ ℚ̄ ⊂ ℂ the real and imaginary parts are algebraic, with h(Re x), h(Im x) ≤ 2·h(x) + 2·log 2 and degree over ℚ at most [ℚ(x):ℚ]². The counting height of a tuple is max_i h(x_i).
hypotheses: Heights are absolute (normalised over ℚ); ℚ̄ is the algebraic closure inside ℂ.
proofSteps: The lower bound compares each place's maximum with |x_i|_w; the upper bound uses max(1, |x₁|, …) ≤ Π max(1, |x_i|) place by place.
Complex conjugation c restricts to an element of Gal(ℚ̄/ℚ), so h(c x) = h(x) by normalized-height Galois invariance.

Re x = (x + c x)/2 and Im x = (x − c x)/(2i): apply h(a + b) ≤ h(a) + h(b) + log 2 and h(ab) ≤ h(a) + h(b) (Mathlib Height.logHeight₁_add_le and Height.logHeight₁_mul_le over a common number field), with h(1/2) = log 2 and h(i) = 0.
Re x and Im x lie in ℚ(x, c x), of degree at most [ℚ(x):ℚ]².
acceptance: x = 1 + i: Re x = Im x = 1 has height 0, while h(x) = (1/2)·log 2.

sources.match: Uses the maximum of the coordinate heights of an algebraic tuple and bounds on the real and imaginary parts of algebraic coordinates; the bounds stated here are proved directly.

nodes.title: Northcott's theorem on projective space
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field and n ≥ 0, D ≥ 1, B ∈ ℝ. (a) {x ∈ ℙⁿ(K) : Projectivization.logHeight x ≤ B} is finite. (b) {x ∈ ℙⁿ(ℚ̄) : [ℚ(x):ℚ] ≤ D and h(x) ≤ B} is finite, where ℚ(x) is the field generated by the ratios of the coordinates. In Mathlib's vocabulary (a) is an instance Northcott (Projectivization.logHeight) for ℙⁿ(K).
hypotheses: K a number field; h the normalised height of normalized-height; degrees over ℚ.
proofSteps: (a) Normalise a coordinate to 1; each affine coordinate x_i has absLogHeight₁ ≤ [K:ℚ]^{-1}·B + bounded, and Mathlib's finite_setOfPred_logHeight₁_le gives finitely many values per coordinate.

(b) Each ratio x_i/x_j has degree ≤ D and height ≤ B (tuple-height-adapters). Its minimal polynomial over ℤ has degree ≤ D and Mahler measure ≤ exp(D·B), hence coefficients bounded by binomial coefficients times exp(D·B): finitely many polynomials, finitely many roots.
(a) also follows from (b) with D = [K:ℚ] and extension-invariance.
acceptance: For K = ℚ, n = 1, B = log 2: the points [a:b] with coprime a, b and max(|a|,|b|) ≤ 2 are [0:1], [1:0], [±1:1], [±2:1], [±1:2]: eight points.

sources.locator: §9, height properties list (Northcott is used in §10 and in the arithmetic case of Theorem 9.15's discussion), author copy pp. 30–35
sources.match: Heights over number fields have finite sets of bounded height and degree (cited from Hindry–Silverman Part B).

sources.locator: Remark on heights in §2.6.4 and §9.5.1 (orientation only)
sources.match: Finiteness of points of bounded height underlies the finiteness theorems quoted there.

nodes.title: Linear changes of coordinates change heights boundedly
nodes.statement: For a generalized global field K and T ∈ GL_{n+1}(K), the function h_{K,n}∘T − h_{K,n} is bounded on ℙⁿ(K̄). More generally, for a linear map A : K^{n+1} → K^{m+1} with trivial kernel, h_{K,m}(Ax) ≤ h_{K,n}(x) + C_A on ℙⁿ(K̄).
hypotheses: T invertible; A injective (so Ax ≠ 0 for x ≠ 0).
proofSteps: Upper bound: Mathlib Height.logHeight_linearMap_apply_le applied over each finite subextension K' ⊇ K, then divided by [K':K] (constants scale exactly by extension-invariance).
Lower bound for T: apply the upper bound to T^{-1}.
acceptance: For T(x₀, x₁) = (x₀, x₀ + x₁) on ℙ¹ the difference is at most log 2 in absolute value.

sources.locator: §9, statement that h_{K,n} − h_{K,n}∘T is bounded for T ∈ Aut(ℙⁿ_K), author copy p. 30
sources.match: Records the boundedness of linear changes of coordinates, with proofs referred to Hindry–Silverman §B and Mumford's Abelian Varieties §4 App. II.

nodes.title: Heights along morphisms to projective space
nodes.statement: Let K be a generalized global field, X a projective K-variety and φ : X → ℙⁿ, ψ : X → ℙᵐ morphisms with φ*O(1) ≅ ψ*O(1). Then h_{K,n}∘φ − h_{K,m}∘ψ is bounded on X(K̄). If f : ℙⁿ → ℙᵐ is a morphism given by forms of degree d without common zero, h_{K,m}∘f = d·h_{K,n} + O(1).
hypotheses: X projective over K; φ and ψ morphisms over K; the isomorphism of line bundles is over K.
proofSteps: Both maps are given by bases of subspaces of H⁰(X, L) for L = φ*O(1) generating L; by linear-change-bounded reduce to φ and ψ given by two generating families of sections of the same L.
Upper bounds: each section of one family is a linear combination of products with the other on an affine cover; Mathlib's Height.logHeight_eval_le gives h∘φ ≤ h∘ψ + C.
Lower bounds: the Nullstellensatz on X writes powers of the sections of one family as combinations of the other (Mathlib Height.logHeight_eval_ge in the case of ℙⁿ), giving the reverse inequality.
acceptance: The Veronese map ℙ¹ → ℙ², [x:y] ↦ [x²:xy:y²], has h∘v = 2h exactly.

sources.locator: §9, functoriality bullet (proved by the Nullstellensatz over K̄), author copy p. 31
sources.match: Functoriality of K-heights for morphisms of projective K-varieties, by the Nullstellensatz.
Comparison of very ample presentations of the same line bundle.

nodes.title: Weil's height machine
nodes.statement: Let K be a generalized global field and X a projective K-variety. There is a unique group homomorphism h_{K,•} : Pic(X) → HeightClass(X(K̄)), L ↦ h_{K,L}, such that for every very ample L with complete linear system embedding ι_L : X → ℙ(H⁰(X, L)), h_{K,L} is the class of h_{K,n}∘ι_L. It satisfies: (a) functoriality h_{K,f*M} = f*h_{K,M} for every K-morphism f : X → Y of projective varieties (pullback of classes, height-pullback); (b) extension [K':K]·h_{K,L} = h_{K',L_{K'}}; (c) positivity off the base locus (height-positivity-base-locus); (d) for L ample and M arbitrary there is c > 0 with |h_{K,M}| ≤ c·h_{K,L} + O(1); (e) for K a number field and L ample, Northcott (northcott-ample).
hypotheses: X projective over K (any closed subscheme of some ℙⁿ_K); Pic(X) is the group of isomorphism classes of line bundles.
proofSteps: Very ample case: define h_{K,L} by ι_L; it is well defined by morphism-height-comparison, and additive since the Segre embedding is exact for heights (Mathlib Height.logHeight_fun_mul_eq).
General L: write L ≅ L₁ ⊗ L₂^{-1} with L₁, L₂ very ample; the class h_{K,L₁} − h_{K,L₂} is independent of the presentation by additivity on very ample bundles (Conrad §9 after (9.1)).
Functoriality: for very ample M on Y, f*M is globally generated, and ι_M∘f is a morphism with (ι_M∘f)*O(1) = f*M; compare with an embedding of f*M ⊗ (very ample) via morphism-height-comparison.
(d): L^{⊗N} ⊗ M^{±1} is very ample for N large, and very ample heights are bounded below.
acceptance: On X = ℙⁿ, h_{K,O(d)} = d·h_{K,n}.
Over K = ℚ and X a conic embedded in ℙ², the restriction of h to X(ℚ̄) represents h_{O(1)|X} and twice h_{O_X(P)} for any point P (O(1)|X ≅ O_X(2P) on X ≅ ℙ¹ over ℚ̄).

sources.locator: §9, (9.1) and the paragraph defining h_{K,L} for arbitrary L, the list of basic properties, author copy pp. 30–31
sources.match: Very ample heights via complete linear systems; extension to Pic(X) by differences; a homomorphism Pic(X) → functions modulo O(1); functoriality, positivity of ample heights, quasi-equivalence and positivity off the base locus.
The construction of the line-bundle height class from very ample differences.

nodes.title: Heights are bounded below off the base locus
nodes.statement: For a projective variety X over a generalized global field K and a line bundle L with base locus B = Supp coker(H⁰(X, L) ⊗ O_X → L), every representative of h_{K,L} is bounded below on X(K̄) ∖ B(K̄). In particular for L ample (some power globally generated) h_{K,L} is bounded below on X(K̄).
hypotheses: X projective; L a line bundle with H⁰(X, L) ≠ 0 for a nonempty complement.
proofSteps: Choose a very ample M with L ⊗ M very ample, a basis (s_i) of H⁰(X, L) and a basis (t_j) of H⁰(X, M). At x ∉ B some s_i(x) ≠ 0, so the products s_i·t_j, part of a generating family of L ⊗ M, do not all vanish at x; comparing the heights of [s_i t_j(x)] and [t_j(x)] place by place gives h_{L⊗M}(x) ≥ h_M(x) − C, that is h_L(x) ≥ −C on X ∖ B (Conrad §9, base-locus property; morphism-height-comparison).
acceptance: On ℙ¹ with L = O(1) the base locus is empty and h ≥ 0.

sources.locator: §9, positivity away from the base locus (last bullet of the list of properties), author copy p. 31
sources.match: States that h_{K,L} is bounded below on (X − B)(K̄) for the base locus B of L.

nodes.title: Northcott for ample line bundles
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field, X a projective K-variety and L an ample line bundle on X. For every representative h of h_{K,L} and all D ≥ 1, B ∈ ℝ, the set {x ∈ X(ℚ̄) : [K(x):K] ≤ D and h(x) ≤ B} is finite. With Mathlib's class: for each D the restriction of h to points of degree ≤ D is Northcott.
hypotheses: K a number field (Northcott fails for function fields with infinite constant field, where constant points have height 0).
proofSteps: Replace L by a very ample power L^{⊗m}: h_{K,L^m} = m·h_{K,L} and the property is insensitive to positive scaling and bounded error (northcott-invariance).
For very ample L the height is h_{K,n}∘ι_L with ι_L a closed embedding, so the set embeds into {y ∈ ℙⁿ(ℚ̄) : degree ≤ D[K:ℚ], h(y) ≤ B'}: finite by northcott-projective.
acceptance: For X = ℙ¹_ℚ and L = O(1) at height ≤ log 2 and degree 1: the eight points of northcott-projective's example.

sources.locator: §9, positivity of ample K-heights, and §10 use of Northcott in the arithmetic case, author copy pp. 31–37
sources.match: Ample heights dominate all heights and points of bounded height and degree are finite over number fields.

nodes.title: Tate's limit
nodes.statement: Let S be a set, φ : S → S a map, d > 1 a real number and f : S → ℝ with |f∘φ − d·f| ≤ C on S. Then f̂(s) = lim_{m→∞} d^{−m} f(φ^m(s)) exists for every s, |f̂ − f| ≤ C/(d − 1), and f̂∘φ = d·f̂. It is the unique function g with g∘φ = d·g and g − f bounded. If f' − f is bounded then f̂' = f̂, so the construction descends to height classes.
hypotheses: Only the bound |f∘φ − d f| ≤ C is assumed; no topology on S.
proofSteps: The telescoping series f + Σ_{m≥0} d^{−(m+1)}(f∘φ^{m+1} − d·f∘φ^m) converges uniformly, with tail bounded by C·d^{−m}/(d−1).
f̂∘φ = d·f̂ by shifting the index; uniqueness: if g, g' both satisfy the functional equation with bounded difference D, then |g − g'| = d^{−m}|g∘φ^m − g'∘φ^m| ≤ d^{−m}D → 0.
acceptance: S = ℕ, φ = id, d = 2, f = 1: f̂ = 0 and the bound C/(d−1) = 1 is attained.

sources.match: Canonical heights are limits h(na)/n² and h(na)/n, independent of the representative chosen for h_{K,L}.
Tate's limit for elliptic curves, ĥ = lim h(2ⁿP)/(2·4ⁿ), with convergence proved rather than assumed.

nodes.title: The Néron–Tate canonical height
nodes.statement: Let A be an abelian variety over a generalized global field K and L a line bundle on A. For symmetric L ([−1]*L ≅ L) put ĥ⁺_{K,L} = Tate limit of h_{K,L} along [2] with d = 4; for antisymmetric L ([−1]*L ≅ L^{−1}) put ĥ⁻_{K,L} = Tate limit along [2] with d = 2; in general ĥ_{K,L} = (ĥ⁺_{K,L⁺} + ĥ⁻_{K,L⁻})/2 with L^± = L ⊗ [−1]*L^{±1}. Then ĥ_{K,L} : A(K̄) → ℝ represents h_{K,L}, depends only on the isomorphism class of L, is additive in L, vanishes at 0, is a quadratic form for symmetric L and additive for antisymmetric L, satisfies ĥ_{K,f*M} = ĥ_{K,M}∘f − ĥ_{K,M}(f(0)) for every morphism f : A → B of K-varieties and ĥ_{K,t_a*L} = ĥ_{K,L}∘t_a − ĥ_{K,L}(a), scales by [K':K] under finite extension, and for symmetric L depends only on the algebraic equivalence class of L. For K a number field the absolute Néron–Tate height is [K:ℚ]^{-1}·ĥ_{K,L}.
hypotheses: A an abelian variety over K (Tau Ceti TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety); L any line bundle.
Symmetric: [2]*L ≅ L^{⊗4}; antisymmetric: [2]*L ≅ L^{⊗2} (theorem of the cube).
proofSteps: Theorem of the cube (AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A1.5) gives [2]*L ≅ L⁴ (symmetric) or L² (antisymmetric); with the height machine, h_{K,L}∘[2] − d·h_{K,L} is bounded, so tate-limit applies.
Quadraticity: the parallelogram law holds up to O(1) by the cube theorem on A × A; Tate limits turn it into an identity.
Functoriality and translation: both sides are functions of degree ≤ 2 in the same class modulo O(1), hence differ by a constant, fixed at 0 (Conrad (9.5)–(9.7)).

Algebraic equivalence: for symmetric L, L' with L' ⊗ L^{-1} ∈ Pic⁰(A), M = L' ⊗ L^{-1} is symmetric and antisymmetric, so M² is trivial and ĥ_M is additive with 2ĥ_M = 0 (alternative to Conrad Theorem 9.8's quasi-equivalence argument; Gao–Ge–Kühne Lemma 2.3).
acceptance: ĥ_{K,L}(n a) = n²·ĥ_{K,L}(a) for symmetric L and every integer n.

nodes.title: Positivity and kernel of the Néron–Tate height
nodes.statement: Let A be an abelian variety over a number field K and L a symmetric ample line bundle. Then ĥ_{K,L} ≥ 0 on A(ℚ̄); ĥ_{K,L}(a) = 0 if and only if a is a torsion point; and for every D the set of torsion points of degree ≤ D over K is finite. The proof uses Northcott only, not the finite generation of A(K).
hypotheses: K a number field; L symmetric and ample.
proofSteps: Non-negativity: h_{K,L} is bounded below (height-positivity-base-locus), so the quadratic form ĥ_{K,L} is bounded below, hence ≥ 0 (Conrad §9 after Lemma 9.7).
If ĥ(a) = 0, all multiples n•a lie in A(K(a)) and have ĥ = 0, hence bounded h_{K,L}: finitely many by northcott-ample, so a is torsion. Conversely ĥ(a) = m^{−2}ĥ(m•a) = 0 for m the order.
Finiteness of torsion of bounded degree: Mathlib's Monoid.finite_set_isOfFiniteOrder_of_descent (additive form) applied to A(K') for each K' of degree ≤ D, together with Northcott for bounded degree.
acceptance: For an elliptic curve this specialises to Tau Ceti's WeierstrassCurve.Affine.Point.canonicalHeight_eq_zero_iff_isOfFinAddOrder.

sources.locator: §9, sentence after Lemma 9.7 (ĥ ≥ 0 for symmetric ample L) and the arithmetic case before Theorem 9.15, author copy pp. 33–35
sources.match: Non-negativity of ĥ_{K,L} for symmetric ample L and positive definiteness over classical global fields.

Its real extension is positive semidefinite on A(K')_ℝ for L ample.
hypotheses: L symmetric; K generalized global field.
proofSteps: Bilinearity from the parallelogram law of a quadratic form (Mathlib QuadraticMap.polarBilin).
Comparison with φ_L: Conrad Theorem 9.10 via the Poincaré bundle and functoriality.
Semidefiniteness from ĥ ≥ 0 (Conrad Corollary 9.12).
acceptance: For E elliptic and L = O(O): ⟨P, P⟩_L = 2ĥ(P), compared with Tau Ceti's neronTatePairing.

nodes.title: Local Weil functions and Néron functions
nodes.statement: For a place v of a generalized global field K and a Cartier divisor D on a projective K-variety X, a local Weil function λ_{D,v} : X(K̄_v) ∖ |D| → ℝ is a function such that locally D = div(f) with λ_{D,v} + log|f|_v extending to a locally bounded continuous function; it is unique up to a bounded continuous function, additive in D and functorial for pullbacks; sums Σ_v n_v λ_{D,v}, taken over a family that is M_K-bounded, represent h_{K,O(D)}. On an abelian variety A with D symmetric (or antisymmetric), the Néron function λ̂_{D,v} is the unique local Weil function, up to an additive constant, with λ̂_{D,v}([2]x) = 4λ̂_{D,v}(x) − log|g(x)|_v + c_v (respectively with 2 in place of 4) for a rational function g with div g = [2]*D − 4D (respectively [2]*D − 2D) and a constant c_v, and the canonical height decomposes as ĥ_{K,O(D)}(x) = Σ_v n_v λ̂_{D,v}(x) for x ∉ |D|.
hypotheses: D a Cartier divisor; v a place of K; normalisations follow the M_K-field normalisation of generalized-global-field.
proofSteps: Existence via presentations of D as a difference of base-point-free divisors (Bombieri–Gubler Chapter 2, as cited by Gubler 2007 §2).
Néron functions: Tate's limit applied to λ_{D,v} along [2] with correction log|g|_v (Bombieri–Gubler Theorems 9.5.4 and 9.5.7, cited in Gubler 2007 §2.10).
Decomposition: the product formula kills the constants Σ_v n_v c_v.
acceptance: For A = E an elliptic curve and D = (O), λ̂_{(O),v} is the classical Néron local height.

nodes.title: Multiplication by two is given by quartic forms
nodes.statement: Let A be an abelian variety over a field, embedded in ℙⁿ by the complete linear system of a symmetric very ample L such that the embedding is projectively normal. Then [2] : A → A is given by homogeneous polynomials f₀, …, f_n of degree 4 without common zero on A. Consequently h∘[2] = 4h + O(1) is exhibited by explicit forms, and [2^l] is given by forms of degree 4^l.
hypotheses: L symmetric and very ample, the embedding projectively normal.
proofSteps: [2]*L ≅ L^{⊗4}; projective normality makes H⁰(ℙⁿ, O(4)) → H⁰(A, L^{⊗4}) surjective, so the pulled-back coordinates are restrictions of quartics; they have no common zero since [2] is a morphism (Serre, in Waldschmidt Appendix II, Corollary 2, as cited by Dimitrov–Gao–Habegger).
acceptance: For an elliptic curve E embedded in ℙ³ by the symmetric very ample bundle O(4·O), duplication is given by four quartic forms in the coordinates.

sources.locator: proof of Proposition 4.3, pp. 19–20, (4.11), citing Waldschmidt 1987
sources.match: On a projectively normal abelian variety embedded by a symmetric very ample bundle, [2] is given by quartic forms without common zeros on A; iterates by forms of degree 4^l.
The same description in families after removing finitely many base points.

nodes.title: The Silverman–Tate theorem in families
nodes.statement: Let S be a regular irreducible quasi-projective variety over ℚ̄ with a projective compactification S ⊆ S̄ ⊆ ℙᵐ, π : 𝒜 → S an abelian scheme with a closed immersion 𝒜 → ℙⁿ × S, and L = O(1,1)|_𝒜 symmetric on the generic fibre. There is c > 0 with |ĥ_{𝒜_{π(P)}}(P) − h(P)| ≤ c·max{1, h_{S̄}(π(P))} for all P ∈ 𝒜(ℚ̄), where ĥ is the fibrewise Néron–Tate height of L and h the height on ℙⁿ × ℙᵐ.
hypotheses: Abelian scheme over a regular quasi-projective base over ℚ̄; L the restriction of O(1,1), symmetric on the generic fibre; line bundles rather than Weil divisors, so no smoothness of S̄ is needed.
proofSteps: Duplication estimate (family-duplication-estimate) gives |h([2]P) − 4h(P)| ≤ c₁·max{1, h_{S̄}(π(P))}.
Telescoping as in tate-limit with a base-dependent constant gives the bound with c = c₁/3.
acceptance: For a constant family A × S → S the error term is bounded independently of h_S.

sources.match: A Cartier-divisor version of Silverman's Theorem A (Crelle 342).
The line-bundle version with error c₁(1 + h(π(P))), the smoothness hypothesis of Silverman's original removed.

nodes.title: The duplication estimate in families
nodes.statement: In the situation of silverman-tate there is c₁ > 0 with |h([2]P) − 4h(P)| ≤ c₁·max{1, h_{S̄}(π(P))} for all P ∈ 𝒜(ℚ̄).
hypotheses: As in silverman-tate.
proofSteps: Close the graph of [2] to 𝒜'; F' = [2]*L ⊗ L^{⊗−4} is trivial on the generic fibre, hence a pullback from S up to boundary divisors.
Resolve S̄ and the closure of 𝒜 (Hironaka) and bound a Cartier divisor supported over the boundary by pullbacks of effective divisors avoiding a given π(P); finitely many choices cover S.
Compare heights on the resolution with h_{S̄} by the Height Machine on the projective base.
acceptance: For a constant family the estimate holds with h_{S̄} replaced by 1.

sources.match: The duplication estimate with constant c₁·max{1, h_{S̄}(π(P))}; the last comparison of heights on the resolution needs the argument recorded in the paper's source issue E10.

nodes.title: The fibrewise Néron–Tate height depends only on the generic fibre
nodes.statement: Let π : 𝒜 → S be an abelian scheme over an irreducible base and L, L' line bundles on 𝒜 whose restrictions to the generic fibre are both isomorphic to L₀^{⊗l}. Then L' ⊗ L^{-1} is the pullback of a line bundle on S, so L|_{𝒜_s} ≅ L'|_{𝒜_s} for every s and the fibrewise Néron–Tate heights agree; ĥ_{𝒜,L₀} depends only on L₀.
hypotheses: S irreducible (normal for the descent of line bundles); l ≥ 1.
proofSteps: A line bundle on 𝒜 trivial on the generic fibre is a pullback from S (EGA IV 21.4.13 / the seesaw principle with rigidification, AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A1.4), so fibres agree.
neron-tate-height depends only on the isomorphism class on each fibre.
acceptance: Twisting L by π*M for M on S does not change any fibrewise height.

sources.match: Model independence of the fibrewise normalisation, via EGA IV 21.4.13.

nodes.title: Silverman's height limit theorem
nodes.statement: Let S be a smooth projective curve over ℚ̄ with function field K = ℚ̄(S), π : 𝒜 → S° an abelian scheme over a dense open S° with generic fibre A/K, L symmetric ample. For x ∈ A(K̄) represented by a section σ_x : S' → 𝒜 over a generically finite ρ : S' → S, ĥ_{𝒜_{ρ(t)}}(σ_x(t)) / h_S(ρ(t)) → ĥ_{K,A}(x) as h_S(ρ(t)) → ∞, with h_S = h∘ι/deg S for an embedding ι and ĥ_{K,A} the function-field Néron–Tate height (geometric-height-field structure on K). Heights on curves are quasi-equivalent: h_S∘ρ/h_{S'} → deg ρ, and ĥ_{K',A_{K'}} = [K':K]·ĥ_{K,A}.
hypotheses: S a smooth projective curve over ℚ̄; the abelian scheme over a dense open subset; L symmetric ample on the generic fibre.
proofSteps: Silverman's Theorem B (Crelle 342) as presented by Gao–Habegger Theorem 11.1, using Bombieri–Gubler Corollary 9.3.10 and Conrad Remark 9.2 for the base change of function-field heights.
acceptance: For a constant family A₀ × S with x a constant point, both sides are 0.

sources.match: Silverman's height limit theorem after base change, with the quasi-equivalence of heights on curves and the degree scaling of function-field Néron–Tate heights (the paper's misprints E16 corrected).

nodes.title: Heights under generically finite dominant maps
nodes.statement: Let f : X' → X be a dominant generically finite morphism of varieties over ℚ̄ (or an equidimensional dominant rational map), with heights h' and h from ample line bundles on projective compactifications. There are c > 0, c' and a dense Zariski open U ⊆ X' with h(f(P)) ≥ c·h'(P) − c' for P ∈ U(ℚ̄). The inequality holds only on U: it is not a global two-sided comparison.
hypotheses: X', X varieties over ℚ̄; f dominant and generically finite.
proofSteps: Silverman 2011 (J. Ramanujan Math. Soc. 26), as cited by Gao–Habegger: compare f*L with an ample bundle on a blow-up and apply height-positivity-base-locus off the exceptional locus.
acceptance: For f : ℙ¹ → ℙ¹, x ↦ x², U = ℙ¹ and c = 2.

sources.locator: proof of Proposition 9.1, p. 49, citing Silverman 2011
sources.match: The lower bound on a dense open subset; the paper's application needs instead a global comparison under base change (its source issue E25).

nodes.title: Heights of subvarieties over polarized function fields
nodes.statement: Let K/k be finitely generated with k algebraically closed, (S, M) a polarization of K/k, A an abelian variety over K with a symmetric ample line bundle L, and (𝒜, π, ℒ) an integral model over S (𝒜 projective over k, π : 𝒜 → S projective with generic fibre A, ℒ extending L). For a closed subvariety X ⊆ A with closure 𝒳 ⊆ 𝒜, the naive height is h_{(𝒜,ℒ)}(X) = (ℒ^{dim X+1} · (π*M)^{dim S−1} · 𝒳) / ((1 + dim X)·deg_L X). The canonical height ĥ_L(X) = lim n^{−2} h_{(𝒜,ℒ)}([n]X) exists, depends on (S, M) and L but not on the model, is ≥ 0, and for a point x it is the Néron–Tate height ĥ_{K,L}(x) of the geometric-height-field structure. For X' ⊆ A_{K̄}, ĥ(X') := ĥ of its image in A.
hypotheses: K/k finitely generated with trdeg ≥ 1 and k algebraically closed; integral models exist after shrinking S (spreading out).
proofSteps: Intersection numbers on 𝒜 from SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.5; existence of the limit and independence of the model by Gubler's theory of canonical heights over M-fields (Gubler 2007 Theorem 3.4 and §3.5–3.6; Gubler 2003 Theorem 11.18).
Non-negativity: take ℒ ample (Xie–Yuan (1.2)–(1.3)).
Points: model-mk-height-comparison identifies the point case with ĥ_{K,L}.
acceptance: When trdeg K/k = 1, S is the unique smooth projective model and M plays no role.

nodes.title: Laws for function-field canonical heights
nodes.statement: For A over K = k(S) with polarization (S, M): point canonical heights are additive in symmetric line bundles, satisfy ĥ_{φ*L}(x) = ĥ_L(φ(x)) for homomorphisms φ, and ĥ_{p₁*L₁⊗p₂*L₂}(x, y) = ĥ_{L₁}(x) + ĥ_{L₂}(y); for symmetric ample L, L' there are c, C > 0 with c·ĥ_L ≤ ĥ_{L'} ≤ C·ĥ_L on A(K̄). For cycles, the unnormalised mixed canonical height H_{L₀,…,L_d}(Z) is multilinear and H_{φ*L₀,…,φ*L_d}(Z) = H_{L₀,…,L_d}(φ_*Z); when φ|_Z is generically finite onto its image of dimension d the degree factor cancels in the normalised height. Changing the ample base polarization (on a common projective model) changes heights by two-sided bounded factors and preserves density of small points.
hypotheses: K = k(S) with S normal projective over algebraically closed k and M ample; L, L' symmetric ample.
proofSteps: Point laws: neron-tate-height applied to the geometric-height-field structure.
Comparison: L'^{⊗N} ⊗ L^{−1} and L^{⊗N} ⊗ L'^{−1} are ample for N large, and canonical heights of ample symmetric bundles are ≥ 0.
Cycle laws: Gubler 2003 Theorem 11.18(a)–(e) and Gubler 2007 §§2.10, 3.1–3.6 for mixed heights; projection formula (SF.5).
acceptance: For φ = [n], ĥ_{[n]*L} = n²ĥ_L for symmetric L.

sources.match: Uses functoriality, products and comparison of canonical heights of points and subvarieties.
Mixed canonical heights over function fields with their multilinearity and functoriality.

nodes.title: Function-field heights under finite and constant field extensions
nodes.statement: Let K = k(S) with S a smooth projective curve over algebraically closed k, and K'/K finite with S' the normalisation of S in K'. Recomputing heights with the model S' gives ĥ_{S'}(x) = [K':K]·ĥ_S(x), and the same scaling for subvarieties with pulled-back line bundles; the degree includes the inseparable degree. Under an extension l/k of algebraically closed fields, intersection numbers of base-changed proper schemes and canonical heights of geometrically integral subvarieties are unchanged. Consequently density of small points is invariant under finite extension of K and extension of algebraically closed constants.
hypotheses: S a smooth projective curve; k algebraically closed; k ⊆ l algebraically closed.
proofSteps: Points: projection formula for S' → S and [K'(x):K] = [K'(x):K'][K':K] (Conrad Lemma 8.6 and Remark 9.2).
Subvarieties: projection formula for intersection numbers under finite maps (SF.5).
Constant extension: intersection numbers are invariant under flat base change of the ground field.
acceptance: Distinguish: enlarging only the field of definition of x inside one normalised height does not change ĥ; recomputing with S' multiplies by [K':K].

sources.match: Uses the behaviour of the geometric heights under finite and constant extensions.
The exponent [k':k] relating the algebraic-method structure and the model structure, and the extension formula for heights.

nodes.title: Model heights are M_K-field heights
nodes.statement: For K = k(S), S normal projective over algebraically closed k and M ample, give K the geometric-height-field structure of (S, M). For a projective K-variety X with a line bundle L and a projective model (𝒳, ℒ) over S, the model intersection height of points and subvarieties equals the M_K-field height with model metrics, up to bounded functions for points; Tate's limit identifies the canonical height of geometric-subvariety-height with the canonical-metric Néron–Tate height H_L(X)/((dim X + 1)·deg_L X). For S a curve the closed-point weights are 1 and the formula agrees with the function-field point height of Gao–Habegger §2.1, including the denominator [K(x):K].
hypotheses: As in geometric-height-field; models projective over S.
proofSteps: Gubler 2007 Theorem 3.4(e) identifies model heights and sums of local heights; Theorem 3.6(d) with the Tate limit identifies canonical heights; keep the unnormalised mixed height until the final division.
acceptance: For X = ℙⁿ_K with its standard model ℙⁿ_S the model height of a point is h_{K,n}.

sources.match: Defines heights by intersection numbers on models.
Identifies model heights with sums of local heights over the M_K-field of a polarized function field, and canonical heights via Tate's limit.
Heights over the function field of a curve with the product formula, independent of the field of definition.

nodes.title: Canonical heights under everywhere good reduction
nodes.statement: Let S be a smooth projective curve over algebraically closed k, K = k(S), A/K with everywhere good reduction and 𝒜 → S the abelian scheme extending it. A symmetric ample L on A extends to a symmetric rigidified ℒ on 𝒜, and for every closed subvariety X ⊆ A with closure 𝒳, h_ℒ(X) = ℒ^{dim X+1}·𝒳/((dim X + 1)·deg_L X) satisfies h_ℒ([n]X) = n²·h_ℒ(X); hence it equals ĥ_L(X).
hypotheses: Everywhere good reduction over a complete curve S.
proofSteps: Extend a divisor of L and subtract π*e*ℒ' to rigidify; symmetry follows from rigidification since ℒ − [−1]*ℒ is a pullback from S (fibrewise-height-model-independence) and trivial along the zero section.
[n]*ℒ ≅ ℒ^{⊗n²} on 𝒜 by the cube theorem over S (AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A1.5); the projection formula gives the scaling.
acceptance: For a constant abelian variety A = A₀ × S, h_ℒ(X) = 0 for constant X.

sources.match: The canonical height of a subvariety equals the intersection-theoretic height for the symmetric rigidified extension under everywhere good reduction.

nodes.title: Kummer maps of isogenies of abelian varieties
nodes.statement: Let φ : A → B be an isogeny of abelian varieties over a field K with kernel A[φ] (a finite commutative K-group scheme). The fppf exact sequence 0 → A[φ] → A → B → 0 gives the Kummer map δ_φ : B(K)/φ(A(K)) ↪ H¹_fppf(K, A[φ]), an injective group homomorphism, natural in K and in φ, whose value at b is the class of the A[φ]-torsor φ^{-1}(b). When deg φ is prime to char K, A[φ] is étale and H¹_fppf(K, A[φ]) = H¹(G_K, A[φ](K^sep)) (continuous cohomology with the discrete module), so δ_φ is the Galois Kummer map; for φ = [n] it is A(K)/nA(K) ↪ H¹(K, A[n]).
hypotheses: φ an isogeny (finite flat surjective homomorphism); fppf cohomology of a field.
Galois description only when deg φ is invertible in K.
proofSteps: φ is finite flat and surjective, hence an fppf epimorphism of sheaves; the long exact sequence of fppf cohomology over Spec K gives B(K) → H¹(K, A[φ]) with kernel φ(A(K)) (SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.2 sheaf cohomology; torsor description SF.1/torsor-cohomology).
The evaluation description: the fibre φ^{-1}(b) is an A[φ]-torsor over K and its class is δ_φ(b) (Poonen §8.4, proof of Theorem 8.4.9: the two maps coincide).
Étale case: A[φ] étale and étale = Galois cohomology over a field.
acceptance: For E : y² = x³ − x over ℚ and φ = [2], δ(0,0) is the class of the 2-covering obtained by halving (0,0), nonzero since (0,0) ∉ 2E(ℚ).

sources.match: For m prime to char k, the exact sequence 0 → A[m] → A → A → 0 of étale sheaves gives A(k)/mA(k) ↪ H¹(k, A[m]), and this coincides with evaluating the A[m]-torsor [m]: A → A.
Isomorphism classes of fppf G-torsors are classified by H¹_fppf.

nodes.title: Local Kummer images at places of good reduction
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field, A/K an abelian variety, n ≥ 1, and v a finite place of K with v ∤ n at which A has good reduction. Then the image of A(K_v)/nA(K_v) in H¹(K_v, A[n]) is the unramified subgroup H¹_nr(K_v, A[n]) = H¹(G_{k_v}, A[n](K_v^nr)); in particular every class in the image becomes trivial on the inertia group I_v.
hypotheses: Good reduction at v: A extends to an abelian scheme over O_v (its Néron model); v ∤ n.
proofSteps: The Néron model is the abelian scheme 𝒜/O_v (NeronModels R11.1/abelian-scheme-model); A[n] is finite étale over O_v, so I_v acts trivially (Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich, R11.5).
Over K_v^nr, [n] is surjective on 𝒜(O_v^nr) by Hensel's lemma (smooth [n] with surjective reduction on the special fibre), so the image of the Kummer map restricted to I_v vanishes.

Conversely an unramified class is the class of an étale A[n]-torsor over O_v, which has a point over the finite residue field by Lang's theorem and lifts by Hensel (Poonen Theorem 6.5.13 Step 2 argument).
acceptance: For E/ℚ with good reduction at p odd and n = 2, the local image at p is H¹_nr(ℚ_p, E[2]) of order #E(ℚ_p)[2].

sources.match: For v outside S, points over k_v of a proper model give torsor classes coming from H¹(O_v, G), by the valuative criterion of properness.
H¹(O_v, F) → H¹(k_v, F) has trivial kernel for finite étale F, and H¹(O_v, G⁰) = 0 for smooth connected G⁰ by Lang and Hensel.

nodes.title: Selmer groups and Tate–Shafarevich groups of abelian varieties
nodes.statement: For an isogeny φ : A → B of abelian varieties over a number field K, the Kummer Selmer structure on A[φ] has local conditions the images of the local Kummer maps δ_{φ,v} : B(K_v)/φA(K_v) → H¹(K_v, A[φ]) at every place v; it is unramified at almost all v (local-kummer-image-unramified) and is a Selmer structure in the sense of TauCetiRoadmap EllipticCurves Layer 7. Sel^φ(A/K) ⊆ H¹(K, A[φ]) is its Selmer group, and Ш(A/K) = ker(H¹(K, A) → Π_v H¹(K_v, A)) with H¹(K, A) the Galois cohomology of the discrete module A(K^sep). For φ = [n] write Sel^n(A/K).
hypotheses: K a number field (characteristic 0, so all cohomology is Galois cohomology); every place, including archimedean ones.
proofSteps: Instantiate the general Selmer-structure constructor of EllipticCurves Layer 7 with M = A[φ](K^sep) and local subgroups the Kummer images.
Ш is the Weil–Châtelet group's locally trivial part, as in EllipticCurves Layer 7 with E replaced by A.
acceptance: For E : y² = x³ − x over ℚ, Sel²(E/ℚ) ≅ (ℤ/2)², equal to the image of E(ℚ)/2E(ℚ) = E[2](ℚ).

sources.match: The Selmer set of a torsor; for an isogeny viewed as a torsor under its kernel it is the classical Selmer group (e.g. the 2-Selmer group of an elliptic curve).
Selmer structures on discrete Galois modules, the Selmer group and Sha, stated generally so that the same API serves abelian varieties.

nodes.title: The descent exact sequence
nodes.statement: For an isogeny φ : A → B over a number field K there is an exact sequence 0 → B(K)/φA(K) → Sel^φ(A/K) → Ш(A/K)[φ] → 0, where Ш(A/K)[φ] is the kernel of φ_* : Ш(A/K) → Ш(B/K).
hypotheses: K a number field; φ an isogeny.
proofSteps: Compare the global and local Kummer sequences place by place (diagram chase), as in EllipticCurves Layer 7 for [m] on an elliptic curve.
acceptance: For E : y² = x³ − x over ℚ and φ = [2]: Ш(E/ℚ)[2] = 0 and B(K)/φA(K) ≅ Sel² ≅ (ℤ/2)².

nodes.title: Finiteness of Selmer groups
nodes.statement: For an isogeny φ : A → B of abelian varieties over a number field K, Sel^φ(A/K) is finite. More precisely, if S contains the archimedean places, the places above deg φ and the places of bad reduction, then Sel^φ(A/K) ⊆ H¹(G_{K,S}, A[φ]), which is finite.
hypotheses: K a number field; S finite as stated.
proofSteps: Outside S the local conditions are unramified (local-kummer-image-unramified), so Sel^φ lies in the image of H¹(G_{K,S}, A[φ]) under inflation.
H¹(G_{K,S}, M) is finite for finite M of order invertible outside S (ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.3/h1-finite, via Hermite's theorem R02.3/hermite-unramified-outside-finite).
Alternative route: the Selmer set of the proper torsor B → B under A[φ] is finite (Poonen Theorem 8.4.6).
acceptance: For φ = [2] on y² = x³ − x, S = {2, ∞} and #H¹(G_{ℚ,S}, E[2]) = #(ℚ(S,2))² = 16 bounds #Sel² = 4.

sources.match: The Selmer set of a torsor over a proper variety over a global field is finite, via H¹_S and Theorem 6.5.13.

nodes.title: The weak Mordell–Weil theorem
nodes.statement: Let A be an abelian variety over a global field K and m ≥ 1 not divisible by char K. Then A(K)/mA(K) is finite. For K a number field this holds for every m ≥ 1.
hypotheses: K a global field; m invertible in K.
proofSteps: A(K)/mA(K) embeds into H¹(K, A[m]) by kummer-map; its image lies in Sel^m(A/K) (Kummer images are locally Kummer images), which is finite by selmer-finite (number fields) or by Poonen Theorem 8.4.6 (global fields).
Over number fields every m is invertible.
acceptance: For an elliptic curve over ℚ this is Tau Ceti's weak Mordell–Weil for m = 2 (TauCetiRoadmap EllipticCurves Layer 6).

sources.match: Weak Mordell–Weil over a global field for m not divisible by the characteristic, via the finite Selmer set.

nodes.title: The Mordell–Weil theorem
nodes.statement: For an abelian variety A over a number field K, the group A(K) is finitely generated. Its torsion subgroup is finite and A(K) ≅ ℤ^r ⊕ A(K)_tors with r = rank A(K).
hypotheses: K a number field.
proofSteps: Choose a symmetric ample L; h = ĥ_{K,L} on A(K) is ≥ 0, satisfies the parallelogram law exactly, and is Northcott on A(K) (northcott-ample, since ĥ represents h_{K,L}).
A(K)/2A(K) is finite (weak-mordell-weil), i.e. the subgroup 2A(K) has finite index.

Mathlib's descent theorem CommGroup.fg_of_descent' in its additive form AddCommGroup.fg_of_descent' gives finite generation; Mathlib Monoid.finite_set_isOfFiniteOrder_of_descent (additive form) gives finite torsion.
acceptance: For an elliptic curve this is Tau Ceti's WeierstrassCurve.Affine.Point fg theorem of EllipticCurves Layer 6 (fg_point_of_numberField).
A(K) need not be finitely generated over K = ℂ(t) when A is constant: A(ℂ) ⊆ A(ℂ(t)) is uncountable (compare lang-neron).

sources.match: The Mordell–Weil theorem for abelian varieties over global fields; the weak theorem is proved on the way.

sources.locator: §7, Theorem 7.1 and Corollary 7.2, author copy pp. 23–24
sources.match: Finite generation of A(K) for K finitely generated over its prime field (number fields included), by the height argument.
Mordell–Weil for elliptic curves by the naive-height descent, already in Tau Ceti.

nodes.title: Positive definiteness of the Néron–Tate height on A(K) ⊗ ℝ
nodes.statement: For an abelian variety A over a number field K and a symmetric ample L, the real extension of ĥ_{K,L} to A(K) ⊗ ℝ is positive definite; equivalently the Gram matrix of ⟨,⟩_L on a basis of A(K)/A(K)_tors is positive definite, and its determinant (the L-regulator) is positive.
hypotheses: K a number field; L symmetric ample.
proofSteps: Finite generation (mordell-weil) makes A(K)/tors a lattice Λ of rank r; ĥ is a quadratic form on Λ with finitely many points of bounded value (Northcott) and kernel exactly the torsion (neron-tate-kernel-number-field).
Minkowski's lemma: a quadratic form on a lattice that is ≥ 0, with finitely many lattice points below every bound, extends to a positive definite form on Λ ⊗ ℝ (Conrad Lemma 10.1).
acceptance: For E/ℚ of rank one with generator P, the Gram matrix is (2ĥ(P)) with ĥ(P) > 0.

sources.locator: §10, Lemma 10.1 and the discussion before Theorem 9.15, author copy pp. 35–37
sources.match: Over classical global fields the canonical height is positive definite on A(K) ⊗ ℝ; Minkowski's lemma on quadratic forms with Northcott.

nodes.title: Chow's K/k-trace
nodes.statement: Let K/k be a primary (for example regular) extension of fields and A an abelian variety over K. The K/k-trace is a pair (Tr_{K/k}(A), τ) of an abelian variety over k and a K-homomorphism τ : Tr_{K/k}(A)_K → A, final among pairs (C, f) with C an abelian variety over k and f : C_K → A. It exists; τ has finite kernel, whose Cartier dual is connected; if char k = 0, τ is a closed immersion. There is a unique abelian subvariety A' ⊆ A with A' = image of τ, and (A/A')^{K/k} = 0. Formation of the trace commutes with separable algebraic extensions of k.
hypotheses: K/k primary (k separably closed in K suffices for the universal property; regular for the base-change statements).
proofSteps: Existence and properties: Conrad Theorem 6.2 (existence via the K/k-image of the dual) and Theorem 6.4 (finite kernel, connected Cartier dual of ker τ, closed immersion in characteristic 0).
Base change: Conrad Theorems 6.8 and 6.12.
acceptance: For A = A₀ ⊗_k K constant, Tr_{K/k}(A) = A₀ and τ = id.

sources.locator: §6, Theorem 6.2, Theorem 6.4, Corollary 6.5, Theorems 6.8 and 6.12, author copy pp. 20–23
sources.match: Existence of the K/k-trace, finiteness of ker τ with connected Cartier dual, closed immersion in characteristic 0, and compatibility with base change.
The trace and trace map with the unique abelian subvariety A' = Tr ⊗ K and (A/A')^{K/k} = 0.
The K/k-trace as a final object; in positive characteristic tr is a purely inseparable isogeny onto its image.

trivial trace is the hypothesis of Northcott and of the geometric Bogomolov conjecture

nodes.statement: Let K/k be a finitely generated regular extension and A an abelian variety over K. Then A(K)/τ(Tr_{K/k}(A)(k)) is a finitely generated abelian group. In particular, if Tr_{K/k}(A) = 0 then A(K) is finitely generated.

proofSteps: Conrad §7: reduce to K/k of transcendence degree one (Lemmas 7.3–7.4) and prove weak Mordell–Weil plus the height descent over the generalized global field of a polarization (Conrad Lemma 7.5 and §9–10); positive definiteness modulo the trace (Theorem 9.15) supplies the Northcott-type input.
acceptance: For E/ℂ(t) with nonconstant j-invariant, E(ℂ(t)) is finitely generated.

nodes.title: Kernel of the Néron–Tate height over function fields
nodes.statement: Let K/k be finitely generated regular with trdeg ≥ 1, made a generalized global field by a polarization (V, N), A/K an abelian variety and L symmetric ample. Then ĥ_{K,L} vanishes exactly on τ(Tr_{K̄/k̄}(A)(k̄)) + A(K̄)_tors, and the induced quadratic form on (A(K)/τ(Tr(A)(k)))_ℝ is positive definite. In particular, if the K/k-trace is trivial, ĥ_{K,L}(x) = 0 iff x is torsion (the Northcott property for trivial trace).
hypotheses: K/k finitely generated regular, trdeg ≥ 1; L symmetric ample.
proofSteps: ĥ vanishes on the trace points (Conrad Lemma 9.13: heights of constant points are bounded).
Positive definiteness modulo the trace (Conrad Theorem 9.15, proved in §10 via Theorem 10.2 and Néron's Lemma 10.3).
Combine with Lang–Néron and finite extensions (Conrad Lemma 9.16, Corollary 9.17).
acceptance: The kernel is τ(Tr(k̄)) + torsion, not (Tr ⊗ K̄)(K̄) + torsion: the latter is the source misprint recorded for Gao–Habegger §1.

sources.match: Néron–Tate heights vanish on trace points and are positive definite modulo the trace.
With trivial trace, canonical height zero means torsion (citing Conrad Theorem 9.15).

nodes.title: Two-coverings of torsors and the class W[2]
nodes.statement: Let J be an abelian variety over a field k and I a J-torsor. A two-covering of I is a J-torsor Y with a morphism π : Y → I such that π(y + a) = π(y) + 2a; π is finite étale of degree 2^{2 dim J}. Isomorphism classes of two-coverings of I form a principal homogeneous space under H¹(k, J[2]) (twisting), nonempty exactly when [I] ∈ 2·H¹(k, J). For I = J the base point is [2] : J → J, and for a ∈ J(k) the two-covering [2]^{-1}(a) has class δ(a) (kummer-map). For the Jacobian J of C : y² = f(x) of genus g over k (char k ≠ 2, f separable of degree 2g + 2) with torsor J¹ = Pic¹_C and hyperelliptic class d, the map J¹ → J² ≅ J, x ↦ 2x − d, is a two-covering of J by J¹; its class W[2] ∈ H¹(k, J[2]) maps to [J¹] ∈ H¹(k, J), and W[2] = 0 iff J¹(k) ≠ ∅.
hypotheses: J abelian over k; for the hyperelliptic statements char k ≠ 2 and f separable of degree 2g + 2.
proofSteps: A two-covering of I is a J[2]-torsor over I compatible with the J-actions; H¹(k, J[2]) acts simply transitively on such classes by contracted product (SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.1 twisting).
For I = J the classes are the Kummer classes, by the evaluation description of kummer-map (Poonen Theorem 8.4.1).
acceptance: If I = J (trivial torsor), [2] : J → J is a two-covering of class 0.

sources.match: Defines two-coverings of J-torsors, their classes in H¹(ℚ, J[2]), the 2-Selmer group as locally soluble two-coverings of J, and the class W[2] of J¹ → J² ≅ J, which maps to 0 in Ш[2] iff J¹(ℚ) ≠ ∅.

nodes.title: W[2] and odd factorisations
nodes.statement: For C : y² = f(x) over a field k of characteristic ≠ 2 with f separable of degree 2g + 2, the points of the class W[2] (as a J[2]-torsor) are the Weierstrass divisor classes e of degree 1 with 2e ≡ d, and these correspond to the odd factorisations f = g·h over k (g, h of odd degree, rational or conjugate over a quadratic extension). Hence W[2] ≠ 0 whenever f has no odd factorisation over k.
hypotheses: char k ≠ 2; deg f = 2g + 2 even; f separable.
proofSteps: J[2] is generated by differences of Weierstrass points; the J[2]-torsor of halves of d is described by subsets of the roots of f of odd size modulo complement (Bhargava–Gross–Wang Proposition 22(4)).
acceptance: f irreducible of degree 6 over ℚ: no odd factorisation, so W[2] ≠ 0.

sources.match: Points of W[2] are degree-one Weierstrass divisors with 2e ≡ d, corresponding to odd factorisations of f.

nodes.title: The 2-Selmer set Sel₂(J¹) and the 2-Selmer set of order k
nodes.statement: For a number field K and a J-torsor I, Sel₂(I) is the set of isomorphism classes of everywhere locally soluble two-coverings of I. For I = J¹ of a hyperelliptic C as in two-coverings, Sel₂(J¹) is empty or a principal homogeneous space for Sel₂(J), and equals the set of elements of Sel₄(J) that map to W[2]. For odd k > 0, the 2-Selmer set of order k is the subset of classes that locally at every place v come from points e_v − ((k − 1)/2)·d with e_v an effective K_v-divisor of degree k.
hypotheses: K a number field; I a torsor under an abelian variety; k odd.
proofSteps: Instance of the Selmer set of a torsor (Poonen Definition 8.4.4) for the J[2]-torsors of two-coverings; the principal homogeneous structure is the twisting action of H¹(K, J[2]) restricted to local solubility.
acceptance: If C(K) ≠ ∅ then Sel₂(J¹) contains the class of the point and is a coset of Sel₂(J).

sources.match: Defines Sel₂(J¹), its relation to Sel₂(J) and Sel₄(J), and the 2-Selmer set of order k.

nodes.title: A complete elliptic 2-descent
nodes.statement: For E : y² = x³ − x over ℚ (S = {2, ∞}): E[2](ℚ) = {O, (0,0), (±1, 0)}; the local images at 2 and ∞ and the unramified conditions elsewhere cut Sel²(E/ℚ) ⊆ H¹(G_{ℚ,S}, E[2]) down to the image of E[2](ℚ), so Sel²(E/ℚ) ≅ (ℤ/2)², Ш(E/ℚ)[2] = 0, rank E(ℚ) = 0 and E(ℚ) = E[2](ℚ) is finitely generated. The Selmer bound is only an upper bound: for the Jacobian of an everywhere locally soluble genus-one curve y² = f(x) with no rational point (Bhargava–Gross–Wang Theorem 10, g = 1), W[2] is a Selmer element outside the Kummer image, so #Sel² > #E(ℚ)/2E(ℚ).
hypotheses: ℚ, S = {2, ∞}; the x − T descent map of Tau Ceti identifies H¹(ℚ, E[2]) with the kernel of the norm on (ℚ^× /ℚ^{×2})³.
proofSteps: Compute the image of the descent map on E[2](ℚ); compute local images at 2 and ∞; intersect (EllipticCurves Layer 6 explicit 2-descent, already formalised in Tau Ceti's Stoll development).
Apply descent-sequence and mordell-weil.
acceptance: rank E(ℚ) = 0 and #E(ℚ) = 4.

sources.match: The explicit 2-Selmer group in the étale algebra, its finiteness, and the rank bound.

nodes.title: Local indices of multiplication by two
nodes.statement: Let A be an abelian variety of dimension g over a local field. If the field is a finite extension F of ℚ_p, A(F) has an open subgroup of finite index isomorphic to O_F^g, so #A(F)/2A(F) = |2|_F^{-g}·#A(F)[2] (normalised absolute value; for F = ℚ_p this is 2^{g} ·#A(ℚ_p)[2] when p = 2 and #A(ℚ_p)[2] otherwise). Over ℝ, #A(ℝ)/2A(ℝ) = #A(ℝ)[2]/2^g; over ℂ the quotient is trivial.
hypotheses: A abelian of dimension g over a local field of characteristic 0.
proofSteps: p-adic: A(F) is a compact commutative p-adic Lie group of dimension g[F:ℚ_p]; the formal group gives an open subgroup ≅ O_F^g (Mattuck); index count for [2] on a group with finite torsion and the open subgroup.
Real: A(ℝ) ≅ (ℝ/ℤ)^g × (ℤ/2)^r as a compact Lie group; count.
acceptance: For E/ℚ₂ with E(ℚ₂)[2] = ℤ/2 × ℤ/2, #E(ℚ₂)/2E(ℚ₂) = 8.

sources.locator: §5.7, abelian varieties over local fields (orientation), p. 138
sources.match: Abelian varieties and their groups of points; the index formula is proved here from the Lie group structure.
A(F) contains an open subgroup isomorphic to O_F^g for an abelian variety over a p-adic field.

nodes.title: Reduction is injective on torsion
nodes.statement: Let A be an abelian variety over a number field K with good reduction at a finite place v of residue characteristic p, absolute ramification index e_v, and 𝒜 the abelian scheme over O_v. The reduction map A(K_v)_tors → 𝒜(k_v) is injective on torsion of order prime to p, and on all torsion if e_v < p − 1. For the Jacobian J of a curve C over ℚ with good reduction at q, the reduction J(ℚ) → J̃(𝔽_q) is a homomorphism compatible with reduction of points and divisors, injective on torsion for q ≥ 3.
hypotheses: Good reduction at v; e_v < p − 1 for the p-part.
proofSteps: The kernel of reduction is the group of O_v-points of the formal group of 𝒜, which is torsion-free in the stated range (formal logarithm converges); the prime-to-p part injects since [n] is étale on 𝒜 (Néron model, NeronModels R11.1/abelian-scheme-model).
acceptance: E : y² = x³ − x has good reduction at 3 and E(ℚ)_tors = ℤ/2 × ℤ/2 injects into Ẽ(𝔽₃), of order 4.

sources.match: Injectivity of reduction on torsion for abelian schemes over unramified-enough bases.

sources.locator: §6.5, Theorem 6.5.13 proof, Step 2 (Lang and Hensel), p. 184
sources.match: Hensel lifting along smooth group schemes over complete DVRs.

nodes.title: The Kummer map of a two-isogeny
nodes.statement: For E : y² = x(x² + cx + d) over ℚ with d(c² − 4d) ≠ 0, the 2-isogeny φ : E → E' with E' : y² = x(x² − 2cx + c² − 4d) and its dual φ' : E' → E: the Kummer map E(ℚ)/φ'(E'(ℚ)) → H¹(ℚ, E'[φ']) ≅ ℚ^×/ℚ^{×2} is (x, y) ↦ x for x ≠ 0, (0, 0) ↦ d, O ↦ 1; the φ'-Selmer group is the set of d₁ ∈ ℚ^×/ℚ^{×2} dividing d up to squares for which v² = d₁u⁴ + cu² + d/d₁ is everywhere locally soluble; its quotient by the image of E(ℚ) is Ш(E'/ℚ)[φ'].
hypotheses: E with a rational 2-torsion point at (0, 0); characteristic 0.
proofSteps: Instance of kummer-map for the degree-two isogeny: E'[φ'] ≅ μ₂ and H¹(ℚ, μ₂) ≅ ℚ^×/ℚ^{×2} (Kummer theory); the fibre of φ' over (x, y) is the quadratic extension ℚ(√x).
Selmer condition: everywhere local solubility of the homogeneous spaces v² = d₁u⁴ + cu² + d/d₁ (descent-sequence).
acceptance: For E : y² = x³ − x (c = 0, d = −1), the image of E(ℚ) is {1, −1} ⊆ ℚ^×/ℚ^{×2}.

sources.match: Selmer groups of isogenies as Selmer sets of the isogeny torsor.

sources.locator: TauCetiRoadmap EllipticCurves, Layer 7 (Selmer groups of an arbitrary isogeny φ and its dual)
sources.match: Isogeny Selmer groups of elliptic curves with their Kummer sequences.

nodes.title: The topology on points with values in a topological algebra
nodes.statement: Let R be a commutative ring, A a commutative R-algebra and B a commutative topological ring which is an R-algebra. The B-valued points of Spec A are Points_R(A, B) := A →ₐ[R] B. The points topology on Points_R(A, B) is the topology induced by the injection Points_R(A, B) → B^A, φ ↦ (φ(a))_{a ∈ A}, where B^A = (A → B) carries the product topology; equivalently, it is the coarsest topology for which every evaluation φ ↦ φ(a), a ∈ A, is continuous. Lean: `TauCeti.Points R A B`, a type synonym of `A →ₐ[R] B` carrying this topology as an instance; no topology instance is put on `A →ₐ[R] B` itself, so no existing instance is overridden.
hypotheses: R and A commutative; B a commutative topological ring with an R-algebra structure. No finiteness of A and no separation axiom on B is assumed in the definition; the separation, closedness and local-compactness statements of RP.2/points-topology-presentation assume them.
proofSteps: Define the topology as TopologicalSpace.induced along the coercion Points_R(A, B) → (A → B), with Pi.topologicalSpace on the target. The coercion is injective (algebra maps are determined by their values), so this is the subspace topology of the image.
Continuity into Points: a map f from a topological space Z is continuous iff every z ↦ f(z)(a) is continuous (induced topology and product topology universal properties).

Functoriality: for g : A′ →ₐ[R] A, φ ↦ φ ∘ g is continuous, because each evaluation of the composite at a′ is the evaluation at g(a′). For a continuous R-algebra map h : B → B′, φ ↦ h ∘ φ is continuous, because each evaluation of the composite is h composed with an evaluation.

Products: Algebra.TensorProduct.liftEquiv identifies Points_R(A ⊗_R A′, B) with pairs (φ, φ′) (the commutation condition is automatic since B is commutative). The map φ ↦ (φ ∘ includeLeft, φ ∘ includeRight) is continuous by functoriality, and its inverse is continuous because each element of A ⊗_R A′ is a finite sum of products a ⊗ a′, whose value (φ(a)φ′(a′) summed) is a continuous function of (φ, φ′) as B is a topological ring.

Examples: for A = R[X], Polynomial.aeval identifies Points_R(R[X], B) with B through φ ↦ φ(X), a homeomorphism since every evaluation is a polynomial function of φ(X). For A = R[X, Y]/(XY − 1), φ ↦ φ(X) is a bijection onto Bˣ, and the points topology corresponds to Mathlib's topology on units (induced by u ↦ (u, u⁻¹), Units.embedProduct), because the points topology is induced by the two evaluations at X and Y = X⁻¹.
acceptance: Every evaluation map is continuous, and a map into Points is continuous iff all its evaluations are.

For A = R[X, Y]/(XY − 1) and B = 𝔸_ℚ, the space is 𝔸_ℚˣ with the topology in which u and u⁻¹ both vary continuously; it is not the subspace topology from 𝔸_ℚ (Conrad §3). A definition through the embedding of Spec A in the affine line would get this wrong.
No presentation of A enters the definition; that any presentation gives the same topology is a lemma (RP.2/points-topology-presentation).

sources.match: Conrad's topological ring R is the value ring B here; his explicit description of the topology is taken as the definition.
The units example of the acceptance cases.

nodes.title: Presentations compute the points topology
nodes.statement: Let R, A, B be as in RP.2/points-topology, n ∈ ℕ and π : R[X₁, …, X_n] → A a surjective R-algebra map (MvPolynomial (Fin n) R), with aᵢ := π(Xᵢ). Then φ ↦ (φ(a₁), …, φ(a_n)) is a topological embedding Points_R(A, B) → Bⁿ whose image is Z(ker π) := {b ∈ Bⁿ : aeval b f = 0 for all f ∈ ker π}. If B is T1, Z(ker π) is closed, so the embedding is closed and Points_R(A, B) is T1; if B is Hausdorff, Points_R(A, B) is Hausdorff; if B is locally compact Hausdorff, Points_R(A, B) is locally compact.
hypotheses: π surjective; for the closedness statements B is T1 (resp. Hausdorff, locally compact Hausdorff).
proofSteps: Bijection onto Z(ker π): an R-algebra map out of the quotient A ≅ R[X]/ker π is determined by the images of the Xᵢ, and b ∈ Bⁿ is the image of such a map iff MvPolynomial.aeval b kills ker π.

Embedding: the map is continuous (n evaluations). Conversely every a ∈ A is π(f) for a polynomial f, and φ(a) = aeval (φ(a₁), …, φ(a_n)) f is a polynomial function of the coordinates, continuous because B is a topological ring; so each evaluation factors continuously through the image, and the points topology is induced from Bⁿ.
Closedness: Z(ker π) = ⋂_{f ∈ ker π} (b ↦ aeval b f)⁻¹{0}, an intersection of closed sets when {0} is closed.
Separation and local compactness pass to subspaces, and closed subspaces of locally compact Hausdorff spaces are locally compact.
acceptance: For A = R[X]/(X² − 2) and B = ℝ, the image is {±√2} ⊂ ℝ, a closed two-point set.
Two presentations of A give homeomorphic zero sets; the homeomorphism is given by polynomial maps in both directions.

sources.match: Independence of the presentation, which the proof deduces from the polynomial expression of every element in the generators.

nodes.title: Changing the value ring
nodes.statement: Let A be a finitely generated R-algebra and h : B → B′ a continuous R-algebra map of commutative topological R-algebras. Then postcomposition Points_R(A, B) → Points_R(A, B′) is continuous. If h is a topological embedding, so is the induced map; if h is moreover a closed (resp. open) embedding, so is the induced map; and if h(B) is discrete in B′, the image of Points_R(A, B) is discrete in Points_R(A, B′).
hypotheses: A finitely generated; h continuous. The source's closed/open clause is stated with the roles of the two rings exchanged (sourceIssues HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructions/E8); the statement here uses the corrected orientation.
proofSteps: Choose a presentation π : R[X₁, …, X_n] → A (A finitely generated). By RP.2/points-topology-presentation both Points spaces embed in Bⁿ and B′ⁿ as the zero sets of ker π, and the induced map is the restriction of hⁿ : Bⁿ → B′ⁿ, since h is an algebra map.

If h is an embedding (resp. closed, open embedding), so is hⁿ, and Points_R(A, B) = hⁿ⁻¹(Points_R(A, B′)) inside Bⁿ, because a tuple satisfies the equations of ker π in B iff its image does in B′ (h injective). Restrictions of (closed, open) embeddings to preimages are (closed, open) embeddings.
Discreteness: hⁿ(Bⁿ) is discrete in B′ⁿ when h(B) is discrete in B′ (finite products of discrete subspaces), and the image of Points_R(A, B) is a subset of it.
acceptance: The inclusion K → 𝔸_K of a number field into its adele ring gives a discrete embedding of the K-points of any affine K-variety into its adelic points (RP.2/rational-points-discrete).
The inclusion of the valuation ring O_v into K_v is an open and closed embedding, so the integral points of an O_v-model are open and closed in the K_v-points.

sources.match: The discreteness clause, stated in the correct orientation in the source.
The closed and open clauses; the printed hypothesis 'R′ closed in R' has the two rings exchanged (sourceIssues E8).

nodes.title: Adelic points of an affine variety
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field, 𝔸_K = NumberField.AdeleRing (𝓞 K) K its adele ring (the product of the infinite adele ring and the finite adele ring), and A a finitely generated commutative K-algebra, the coordinate ring of the affine K-variety X = Spec A. The adelic points of X are X(𝔸_K) := Points_K(A, 𝔸_K) with the points topology (RP.2/points-topology). They come with: the diagonal ι : X(K) = Points_K(A, K) → X(𝔸_K), postcomposition with the algebra map K → 𝔸_K; for each finite place v (a height-one prime of 𝓞 K) the local projection X(𝔸_K) → X(K_v), K_v = v.adicCompletion K, postcomposition with the projection of the finite adeles to their v-component; and for each infinite place w the local projection X(𝔸_K) → X(K_w), K_w = w.Completion. All of these are continuous. Lean: `TauCeti.AdelicPoints K A`, with `diagonal`, `finiteProj v` and `infiniteProj w`.
hypotheses: K a number field; A a finitely generated commutative K-algebra (so X is an affine K-scheme of finite type). Non-affine varieties are not covered by this node (coverage).
proofSteps: Definition: Points_K(A, 𝔸_K). The adele ring is a topological K-algebra (NumberField.AdeleRing is a topological ring with Algebra K).

Diagonal and projections: the algebra map K → 𝔸_K and the projections 𝔸_K → K_v are continuous K-algebra maps (the projection of the finite adeles to a component is RestrictedProduct.evalRingHom, continuous for the restricted-product topology; the infinite part is a product of the K_w). Postcomposition is continuous by RP.2/points-topology.

Product decomposition: since 𝔸_K = K_∞ × 𝔸_K^f, Points_K(A, 𝔸_K) ≃ₜ Points_K(A, K_∞) × Points_K(A, 𝔸_K^f) and Points_K(A, K_∞) ≃ₜ ∏_w X(K_w) (algebra maps into a product are families of algebra maps into the factors; the topologies agree because both are induced by the evaluations).

Hausdorff: 𝔸_K is Hausdorff (Tau Ceti NumberField.AdeleRing.instT2Space), so RP.2/points-topology-presentation makes X(𝔸_K) Hausdorff. Local compactness: the infinite adeles are locally compact (NumberField.InfiniteAdeleRing.locallyCompactSpace), and the finite adeles are locally compact by RestrictedProduct.locallyCompactSpace_of_group once each O_v is compact; compactness of O_v for a number field is not in the pinned libraries (gap), so the local-compactness API item waits for it.
acceptance: X(𝔸_K) is Hausdorff, and X(K) sits in it as a discrete closed subset (RP.2/rational-points-discrete).
For K = ℚ and A = ℚ[X]/(X² + 1), X(𝔸_ℚ) is empty although X(ℚ_p) is nonempty for every p ≡ 1 mod 4, because X(ℝ) is empty.

sources.match: Adelic points as the A-points of X for the adele ring A of the global field k.
